title: replace historical automated VM management configuration
input: The operator inventories assigned VM management profiles and the services they enabled.
action: Automanage historically coordinated supported VM management settings and integrations. The replacement must preserve patching, backup or monitoring responsibilities through supported resource policies and automation.
output: The operations team applies the accepted configuration using its new management workflow.
check: Compare actual VM settings and recovery procedures before removing historical profile management.

title: move a historical landing-zone blueprint to deployment stacks
input: The platform owner exports blueprint definitions, assignments and governed resource dependencies.
action: Blueprints historically assembled governance and deployment artifacts into assignments. Migrate supported resource ownership to deployment stacks and retain policy assignments through their explicit governance mechanisms.
output: The platform deployment applies the reviewed templates and policies without relying on the historical blueprint assignment.
check: Compare resource ownership, locks, policy effects and delete behavior before accepting the replacement.

title: coordinate a release through linked work items
input: The product owner defines a feature, acceptance requirements and assigned engineering tasks.
action: Boards stores and organizes the team's work items, backlog and workflow state. Linked pull requests and builds provide evidence; changing a work-item state does not itself build or deploy the feature.
output: The release owner checks implemented tasks and acceptance evidence before approving the release item.
check: Verify work-item links, permissions and acceptance results rather than closing unfinished work by status alone.

title: move application caching to an accepted Redis-compatible target
input: The application owner inventories cache keys, expiry policy and supported Redis commands.
action: Azure Cache for Redis serves the application's configured cache operations on existing deployments. Migration to a supported target preserves command compatibility and treats authoritative business data separately from disposable cache entries.
output: The backend queries the replacement cache, falls back to its database on a miss and refreshes permitted entries.
check: Test expiry, reconnect behavior, cold-cache load and safe cutover before removing the original endpoint.

title: test application recovery from an approved failure
input: The resilience owner selects a bounded fault, target resources and stop conditions.
action: Chaos Studio injects supported configured faults during the experiment under its authorized identities. The experiment disrupts selected dependencies; it does not automatically prove business resilience or repair application code.
output: The application owner observes recovery and corrects the verified weakness through the normal change process.
check: Confirm blast radius, emergency stop and application recovery using the agreed service-level acceptance criteria.

title: perform a protected cryptographic operation for an application
input: The authorized application supplies a supported cryptographic request and permitted key identifier.
action: Cloud HSM provides the configured hardware-protected key and cryptographic execution boundary. The client uses the supported interface and authorization model; key custody and backup follow the selected deployment requirements.
output: The application consumes the signature or cryptographic result without exporting protected key material.
check: Check key-access denial, supported algorithms, client failover and recovery of required key backups.

title: start an authorized telehealth communication session
input: The healthcare application validates the participant and requests the permitted communication identity or session.
action: Communication Services provides supported calling, chat or messaging capabilities through its selected SDKs and APIs. The application controls participant identity, session authorization and clinical data access.
output: The authorized participants communicate while the healthcare backend retains clinical record ownership.
check: Test token expiry, participant isolation, reconnect behavior and explicit recording consent where recording is enabled.

title: provision flexible compute capacity for a batch workload
input: The batch owner defines acceptable VM sizes, capacity target and spot-versus-regular policy.
action: Compute Fleet acquires and manages the configured pool of supported VM capacity across selected sizes and zones. The batch scheduler assigns actual tasks to available workers and handles interruptions.
output: Workers execute the accepted batch tasks and persist outputs outside disposable compute.
check: Test capacity shortfall, spot eviction, task checkpointing and cleanup of completed worker capacity.

title: record a tamper-evident business acceptance entry
input: The application submits the accepted transaction digest and authorized audit context.
action: Confidential Ledger appends the permitted entry to its protected ledger and supplies supported integrity evidence. The application determines what the digest represents; ledger integrity does not validate the original business transaction.
output: The auditor retrieves the ledger entry and validates its receipt using the supported verification procedure.
check: Test writer permissions, digest reconciliation and independent receipt verification for a known record.

title: attach managed storage to a stateful Kubernetes workload
input: The platform owner defines supported storage pools, capacity and the workload's volume requirements.
action: Container Storage supplies supported storage orchestration for Kubernetes persistent volumes. The configured storage class and claims determine the pod's volume; the database process inside the pod performs actual reads and writes.
output: The stateful workload writes its accepted application state to the mounted persistent volume.
check: Test pod rescheduling, storage capacity, snapshot or backup support and application-consistent restore.
